newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq holds oil talks with foreign firms - paper.
newsitem.headline: Iraq holds oil talks with foreign firms - paper.

text.p: Iraq is conducting talks with foreign firms to develop an Iraqi oilfield in the south of the country, the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya said on Tuesday.
The paper, quoting Munther al-Alousi head of the oil and energy committee at the National Assembly, named the oilfield al-Ahdab near the town of Kut 172 km south of Baghdad.
"The National Assembly was acquainted with the progress of talks with foreign companies to develop al-Ahdab oilfield," the paper said.
The paper gave no details of names of the foreign companies, cost of the project or when work would start.
European and Arab businessmen are currently in the Iraqi capital taking part in a trade fair which Baghdad said was attended by 16 countries and 51 multinational firms.

Jumhouriya said: "The (Assembly's) committee has held two meetings attended by Undersecretary of the Oil Ministry...to discuss operational cost of the project and the value of the contract (with these firms)."

Iraq is under stringent United Nations trade sanctions imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. The curbs include a ban in exports of oil and imports of all goods except for food and medicine, for which Baghdad has little cash to pay.
Under an agreement signed in May with the U.N., Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil in six months to buy humanitarian needs for Iraqis.
The pact was stalled for security concerns in northern Iraq sparked by Baghdad sending troops in August to back one Kurdish faction to fight a rival.
Jumhouriya quoted the head of a Russian concern taking part in the fair, as saying his country was holding talks with Iraq to form a joint Iraqi-Russian company for oil drilling and extracting.
The paper did not elaborate but said that the Russian firm had developed several Iraqi oilfields before the 1991 Gulf War which ejected Iraqi troops out of Kuwait.
